+Formalizes the parts of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
+(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lemma lines
+803-848, proof lines 850-919) that `DampedNormsHomog` left out: the lower
+bounds of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (display at lines 836-841; the
+multiplier class and the Laplace domains at lines 826-834), and the smoothing
+assertions at the end of the lemma (lines 845-847) and of its proof (lines
+915-917). Read with `E:damped-norm-definitions` (lines 782-793) and
+`G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi)` (lines 777-778). `DampedNormsHomog`
+and `WaveGreen` are unchanged; the extended wrappers are new declarations.
+With this module and `DampedNormsHomog`, `WaveGreen`, every assertion of the
+lemma is a Lean conclusion under `H:homog` with nothing supplied
+(`damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave`), with the reading of the smoothing

+Formalized.
+- The lower bounds: `0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta)` (`N1on_nonneg`, for any measure
+  and `a > 0`) and `0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` (`N2onSq_nonneg`, for an s-finite
+  measure with `int (1+norm(xi)^2)^(-1) dmu < infinity`, `mu{0} = 0`,
+  `0 < a < 1`, `theta > 0`, measurable `S`); `damped_multiplier_comparison`
+  states the whole display, both bounds with the integrability of the
+  integrands, for a general measure (the upper bounds are
+  `DampedNormsHomog.N1on_smoothed_mono` and `N2onSq_smoothed_mono`).
+- The multiplier class `IsMultiplier` (measurable, values in `[0,1]`; the
+  TeX's `m : R^d -> [0,1]` measurable, lines 826-827), closed under products
+  (`IsMultiplier.mul`), containing the Gaussian multipliers
+  `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)`, `eta >= 0` (`gaussMult`, `isMultiplier_gaussMult`).
+- The `N_0` mass sentence (lines 846-847, proof lines 916-917): convolution
+  with a probability measure preserves `GreenMass` (`greenMass_conv`), so
+  `N_0` is unchanged and equals `theta^(-2)` (`N0_conv`); instantiated with the
+  Gaussian `gaussKernel v` and the wave Green measures, `d = 1, 2, 3`
+  (`gauss_waveGreen_mass`).
+- Green smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (lines 845-846, proof lines
+  915-916): for a finite `G`, the characteristic function of `p * G`
+  (`p = gaussKernel v`, `v >= 0`) is `e^(-v norm(xi)^2/2) G hat`
+  (`charFun_gaussKernel_conv`), so the product of the transforms is multiplied
+  by `e^(-v norm(xi)^2)` (`charFun_pair_gaussKernel_conv`). Hence the second
+  norm of `p * G` (`N2GreenSq`: `E:damped-norm-definitions` with kernel `K_S`
+  and `G_s hat` the characteristic function of `G_s`) equals the second norm
+  of `G` with spectral measure `e^(-v norm(xi)^2) mu(dxi)` (`N2GreenSq_gauss`,
+  every `d`, `G_s` finite for `s > 0`). Under the Fourier identity
+  `GreenFourier G` (`G_s hat = waveHat s`, lines 777-778) the second norm of
+  `G` is `N2onSq` (`N2GreenSq_eq`) and that of `p * G` is
+  `N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` with `m = e^(-v norm(xi)^2)` (`N2GreenSq_gauss_eq`); in
+  `d = 1` the Fourier identity is proved (`greenFourier_one`, from

+Conventions and junk values. `N2GreenSq` is a complex Bochner integral (the
+TeX's `int G_s hat conj(G_t hat) dmu` is complex before time integration); a
+non-integrable integrand would give the value `0`. `N2GreenSq_gauss` and

+they hold whether or not the integrands are integrable; `fourier_paper` and
+`fourier_one` conclude the integrability of all four outer integrands.

+statement where that matters carries `v >= 0` (`gauss_waveGreen_mass` holds for
+every `v`). `N_0` uses `(G s univ).toReal`, which is `s` under `GreenMass`.

+## SpaceTimePositivity (whole result)
+
+Wave L8, item c1, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpaceTimePositivity.lean`.
+It proves, with nothing supplied, the space-time facts that the deterministic
+proof of the boundedness claim of `P:variational-positive-scores` needs, and
+states narrower forms of two lemmas. TeX at `a284420`:
+`notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` (standing assumptions lines 4-21,
+`E:raw-occupation-definitions` lines 10-18, `L:occupation-raw-square`
+statement lines 23-42 with `E:occupation-raw-identities` lines 33-37 and the
+bound of line 40, proof lines 44-90) and
+`notes/integrated_intrinsic_constant.tex` (`L:positive-raw-embedding`
+statement lines 22-39 with `E:positive-bochner-inclusion` lines 26-30 and
+`E:positive-raw-mean` lines 33-36; `E:positive-local-spatial-bound` lines
+70-73). The cost `v_Psi`, the mean `h_(Psi,s)` and the class `C_pos` are
+reused from `VariationalDilation` (`rawCost`, `mean`, `CPos`: integral forms of
+`E:compact-raw-cost` and `E:compact-raw-mean`). The physical pairing
+`B_Gamma(F,G) = int (int F(x) G(x-y) dx) Gamma(dy)` is
+`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair`. New objects: `stPair` (the pairing of the
+time slices `Phi1(s,.)`, `Phi2(t,.)`) and the space-time form
+`stForm a Gamma Phi1 Phi2 = int_(0,1)^2 |s-t|^(-a) B_Gamma(Phi1(s,.), Phi2(t,.))`,
+a Bochner integral for the product Lebesgue measure on `(0,1)^2`. It is the
+integral of `E:positive-bochner-inclusion` with `G = H_sp` written through
+the physical pairing, and `A(g)` of `E:raw-occupation-definitions` at
+`Phi1 = Phi2 = g^2`. `stFormIter` is the same form as an iterated integral,
+verbatim `OccupationCeilingFinite.stForm`, and `stFormIter_eq` identifies the
+two for continuous compactly supported fields. Every field in the statements
+is a continuous compactly supported real function on `R x R^d`; the TeX's
+fields live in `L^2(I; H_sp)`. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `a < 1` for
+integrability, `0 < a` for positivity (the mixture representation of the
+kernel needs it), local finiteness of `Gamma` in place of the physical
+covariance bound `E:positive-local-spatial-bound`, evenness of `Gamma` for
+symmetry. Integrability of every integrand is a conclusion
+(`stIntegrand_integrable` and the first two conjuncts of the mean
+identities), so no statement holds through Lean's value `0` of a
+non-integrable Bochner integral. Proof route (the TeX works in the completed
+Hilbert spaces `H_sp` and `H_t (x) H_sp`): spatial positivity
+`B_Gamma(Q,Q) >= 0` for continuous compactly supported `Q` by uniform
+approximation with mollified test functions; positivity of `stForm` by writing
+`|s-t|^(-a)` as a positive mixture of rank-one kernels
+(`TimeCompletion.kern_eq_mixture`) and Fubini (`weighted_stPair`);
+Cauchy-Schwarz by the discriminant; the identities by Fubini
+(`spatialPair_eq_conv`, `integral_mean_mul_eq_stForm_swap`). Wrappers:
+`space_time_positivity_homog` (all facts under `H:homog` with `a = alpha0`,
+`Gamma != 0` not assumed); `spaceTimeCS_holds` (the proposition `SpaceTimeCS
+alpha0 Gamma`, whose fields are definitionally those of
+`OccupationCeilingFinite.SpaceTimeCS`; its nonnegativity hypothesis on the
+field is not needed); `occupation_raw_square_cc_paper` and
+`positive_raw_variance_form_paper` with the sections' standing assumptions
+(`H:homog`, `a = alpha0`, `Gamma != 0`; `Gamma != 0` is carried and not used,
+the parameter is named `_hΓ`). Narrower conclusions: for
+`L:occupation-raw-square`, the profile class is continuous compactly
+supported fields `g` in place of the class `O` (no unit-norm condition is
+needed), and only the integral forms are proved (`A(g) >= 0` as a genuine
+integral, the pairing `int_I int h_(Psi,t) g_t^2 = F(Psi, g^2)`, and the bound
+by `sqrt(v_Psi A(g))`); for `L:positive-raw-embedding`, only the variance
+identity `F(Psi,Psi) = v_Psi` with integrability and `v_Psi >= 0`. Not
+formalized: `H_sp`, the map `Q`, `rho_g` in `H_I` and

+Schur bound is `OccupationCeilingFinite.schur_sharp`); the mean identity
+`T_R Psi(s) = B_E(m_R h_(Psi,s))` and the canonical versions of
+`L:positive-raw-embedding`. Supplied inputs: none.

+## SpatialBracket (whole result)
+
+Formalizes `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` (A common spatial-energy bracket) of
+`notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` at `a284420` (statement lines
+252-266, display `E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` lines 256-260, proof lines
+268-300) for the variational value `S_2^pos` in place of `C_2(Gamma,a)`,
+together with the scalar map `E:occupation-scalar-map` (lines 195-203), the
+ceiling value `U_c` of `E:occupation-score-ceiling` (lines 208-216) as a
+function of its constant, the factor `D_zeta` of `E:raw-occupation-energy`
+(lines 99-104), `K_0` (line 94), the number `Delta` of the proof (lines
+275-283) and the numerical counterexample at `zeta = 1` (lines 290-298).
+Standing assumptions (section setup, lines 4-21): `H:homog` as
+`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, `a = alpha0`,
+`q = 4 - alpha`, `k = 3 - alpha`, `m = q/k`, and `Gamma != 0` (lines 20-21).
+Reused, not redefined: `S_c^pos = sSup (VariationalRate.scoreSet alpha0 Gamma c)`
+(`P:variational-positive-scores`, `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex`
+lines 270-284), `VariationalRate.S1Bdd`, `C_pos = VariationalDilation.CPos`,
+`I_Psi = VariationalDilation.integratedRate` (rate = square root of the real
+Rayleigh supremum), `v_Psi = VariationalDilation.rawCost` (integral form),
+`R_sp = SpatialFourLinear.Rsp`, `E_sp = SpatialFourLinear.Esp`,
+`F_0 = SpatialFourLinear.F0`, `M_a = TemporalEquilibrium.mass` and
+`SpatialFourLinear.energyValue` (the right side of `E:spatial-energy-map`).
+
+Supplied input (named, one): `OccupationCeilingK0 alpha alpha0 Gamma`, for
+every `c > 0` and `Psi` in `C_pos`, `c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 <= U_c` with `C_occ`
+replaced by `K_0 R_sp`. It stands for `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling`
+(`E:occupation-score-ceiling`, lines 205-220) combined with
+`C_occ <= K_0 R_sp` of `P:raw-occupation-energy` (lines 92-97), exactly as the
+proof uses them (lines 269-271), and is no stronger: `U_c` increases with its
+constant, and the pointwise form is equivalent to "the value set is bounded
+above and `S_c^pos <= U_c`" because the value sets are nonempty. It is
+discharged in `L8Completed` by `occupationCeilingK0_holds` (from `OccupationCeilingFinite.occupation_ceiling_K0_paper`) (wave item L8-c2, whose
+`K0` and `ceilingValue` have the same bodies as here), whose own input
+`SpaceTimeCS` is `SpaceTimePositivity.spaceTimeCS_holds` (L8-c1); after
+integration the corollary for `S_2^pos` holds with the section's hypotheses
+and nothing supplied. `S1Bdd` is never an input of the headline:
+`intrinsic_spatial_bracket_paper` derives it from the named input
+(`S1Bdd_of_ceiling`, case `c = 1`); only `spatial_bracket_lower_sSup_paper`
+takes it as a hypothesis, and the existential form
+`spatial_bracket_lower_paper` needs neither.
+
+Narrower than the TeX: (1) the corollary is stated for `S_2^pos`, not for
+`C_2(Gamma,a)`; the identification `C_2 = S_2^pos` is
+`T:intrinsic-second-moment` (stochastic, outside Lean), used in lines
+269-273. (2) The comparison `C_2 <= 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) < 2^m F_a(E_(1/2)^O)`
+(lines 261-265) is stated as `S_2^pos <= 2^m F_0(E) < 2^m F_a(E)` with
+`E = energyValue alpha (K_0 R_sp) = D_(1/2) (K_0 R_sp)^(2/(2-alpha))`, which is
+at least `E_(1/2)^O = D_(1/2) C_occ^(2/(2-alpha))`; the class `O` with the
+original kernel, `A(g)`, `C_occ` and `E_zeta^O` (`E:raw-occupation-definitions`)
+are not defined in Lean, and every scalar identity is stated for a real
+constant `C >= 0` (`C > 0` in the ratio identity) in place of `C_occ`.
+(3) The direct zero case `Gamma = 0` (lines 302-308, after the corollary) is
+not formalized; every wrapper carries `Gamma != 0`, the section's standing
+assumption. (4) `I_Psi` and `v_Psi` are the Rayleigh-form rate and the
+integral-form cost, as everywhere in `VariationalRate`.
+`HomogCovariance` is passed whole to the cited wrappers; no field is claimed
+unused. Proof route: as in the TeX for `S_2^pos`. The lower half multiplies
+`E:spatial-static-energy-score` by `2^m`, the existential form through
+`E:variational-score-set-scaling` (dilating one control), the supremum form
+through `E:variational-score-homogeneity`; `Delta > 0` uses the strict
+midpoint convexity of `x log x` (one of the two arguments the TeX names,
+lines 280-283). Junk values: `Fb`, `ceilingValue` and `Dzeta` are total real
+functions; Lean's real power gives meaningless values for a negative base,
+so every statement restricts to `z >= 0`, `C >= 0`, `zeta > 0`. `sSup` of the
+coefficient-two set is used only where its boundedness is proved or
+`S1Bdd` is assumed. Rows marked "auxiliary to the Lean proof route" have no
+manuscript label.

+## SpectralMassIdentity (whole result)
+
+Proves that the spectral-mass constant `R_alpha` of `E:intro-spectral-mass`
+(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lines
+528-532: `B_1` the unit ball of `R^d` and
+`R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`) is exactly the resolvent at
+`1`, `R_Gamma(1) = int mu(dxi)/(1+norm(xi)^2)`, and hence that
+`R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha` for `q > 0`. The second identity is the
+display in the proof of `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
+(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`, lines 149-155). That
+proof cites "the deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
+`L:damped-homogeneous-norms`" (main file, lines 853-860:
+`int mu(dxi)/(a^2+norm(xi)^2) = alpha V a^(alpha-2) int_0^inf u^(alpha-1)/(1+u^2) du`
+with `V = mu(B_1)`) together with `E:intro-spectral-mass`. The value of the
+radial integral, `pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`, is not written in the TeX; it is
+proved here. With the identity, the module states `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
+with the manuscript's constant `R_alpha` (`spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper`),
+so that lemma is now formalized as printed (statement lines 101-111 of
+`integrated_spatial_occupation.tex`, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound` at
+lines 106-109).
+
+Abstractions. `ralpha mu alpha` is the formula of line 531 verbatim, with
+`B_1` the open unit ball `Metric.ball 0 1` (the same expression as the
+hypothesis `hRdef` of the `IntervalScalar` and `IntervalScalarCompleted`
+wrappers). The TeX does not say open or closed; for a locally finite
+`alpha`-homogeneous `mu` with `alpha > 0` the two balls have the same mass,
+but that equality is not stated in Lean and is not needed. `R_Gamma(q)` is
+`SpectralHomog.resolvent mu q`, the Bochner integral of `1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2)`.
+
+Hypotheses. The general theorems (`resolvent_one_eq_ralpha`,
+`resolvent_eq_ralpha`, `hRdef_iff_resolvent`) assume a locally finite `mu`
+with `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` for measurable `A` and `c > 0`
+(`SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`; the sentence of main lines
+851-852) and `0 < alpha < 2`. The `_paper` wrappers assume `H:homog`
+(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`) and nothing else;
+`Gamma = 0` is allowed (then `mu = 0` and both sides are `0`), as in the lemma
+("allowing `Gamma = 0`", line 103). The homogeneity is derived by
+`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, and `0 < alpha < 2` by
+`alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog`. Fields of `H:homog` used by
+`resolvent_eq_ralpha_paper` and `hRdef_iff_resolvent_paper` (checked against
+every lemma they call: `alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog`,
+`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, `resolvent_one_eq_ralpha`,
+`resolvent_eq_ralpha`): `alpha_range`, `alpha0_pos`, `threshold`, `mu_radon`,
+and `mu_tempered`, `spectral`, `scaling` (through
+`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Carried but unused by these two: `dim`,
+`alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`,
+`Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`. `spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper` uses the
+fields of `SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound_paper` (listed in that
+section: `dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `threshold`, `Gamma_radon`, `mu_radon`,
+`spectral`, `mu_tempered`, `scaling`) and `alpha_range`; carried but unused:
+`alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`.
+Supplied inputs: none.
+
+Implicit hypotheses made explicit, and junk values. The integrability of
+`1/(1+norm(xi)^2)` (and of `1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2)`) against `mu` is a conjunct of
+each identity, so no identity holds through the Lean value `0` of a
+non-integrable Bochner integral; this is the TeX's "`< infinity`" of line 154.
+`mu(B_1) < infinity` by local finiteness, so `(mu(B_1)).toReal` is not a junk
+value, and `sin(pi alpha/2) > 0` for `0 < alpha < 2`, so the division is
+genuine. `ralpha` itself is defined for all real `alpha`; outside `(0,2)` it
+is only a formula and no theorem here uses it there.
+
+Proof route (differs from the TeX, same conclusion). The TeX uses polar
+coordinates. Lean uses the layer-cake formula (as in
+`SpectralHomog.integrable_inv_one_add_sq`, which proves finiteness): for
+`0 < t < 1` the level set `{1/(1+norm(xi)^2) > t}` is the open ball of radius
+`sqrt((1-t)/t)` (`levelset_eq_ball`; empty for `t >= 1`), whose mass is
+`((1-t)/t)^(alpha/2) V` (`SpectralHomog.measure_ball`), and the real Beta
+integral `int_0^1 t^(-a) (1-t)^a dt = a pi/sin(pi a)` for `0 < a < 1`
+(`beta_real`, from Mathlib's complex Beta function and the reflection formula)
+at `a = alpha/2`. `R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1)` is
+`SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog`. Route-only helpers are "no direct label
+(auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".
+
+Consequences recorded here. `hRdef_iff_resolvent(_paper)`: the hypothesis
+`R = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` carried by the `IntervalScalar` and
+`IntervalScalarCompleted` wrappers is equivalent to `R = R_Gamma(1)`; those
+wrappers are unchanged. The general form of `L:spatial-fourier-bound` with
+constant `R_Gamma(1)` stays `SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound` and
+`spatial_fourier_bound_paper`. Not formalized: nothing of
+`E:intro-spectral-mass` or of the display at lines 149-155 is left out.
+
+Refutations (`refutations/spectral-mass-identity/`): `SinFactorTwo`
+(`sin(pi alpha/2)` instead of `2 sin(pi alpha/2)` in `R_alpha`, with `mu`
+Lebesgue on `R^1`, `alpha = 1`), `ExponentSign` (`q^(2-alpha)` instead of
+`q^(alpha-2)`, same `mu`, `q = 2`), `AlphaPositive` (the identity without
+`alpha > 0`, at `mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`, where `R_Gamma(1) = 1` and
+`R_0 = 0`), `FourierBoundAlphaZero` (the `R_alpha` form of the bound under
+the general theorem's hypotheses without `alpha > 0`, with `Gamma` Lebesgue,
+`mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`; outside `H:homog`). `AlphaPositive` and
+`FourierBoundAlphaZero` evaluate `R_0` with denominator `2 sin 0 = 0`, but the
+numerator is `0` as well, so `R_0 = 0` under any reading of the quotient.

+## StaticPhaseCauchy (whole result)
+
+Formalizes the complex-analytic, scalar and Banach-space steps of the proof
+of `P:static-phase-all-orders` (All regularized static phase orders) of
+`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420` (main TeX;
+statement lines 2577-2605, proof lines 2607-2683; all line numbers in this
+section refer to that file). The proposition is an operator and stochastic
+statement. Every row below is either a step proved with nothing supplied or
+a step row of `E:all-static-phase-orders` (lines 2589-2595) or
+`E:all-static-phase-sum` (lines 2599-2604) whose operator and Gaussian
+inputs are supplied hypotheses (class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker
+than the labelled statement). It extends the existing proof-step rows of
+`SeriesType` for this proposition (the elementary series bound of lines
+2670-2679), which `all_static_phase_sum_step` uses.
+
+Constants (nothing supplied): `I_a` and `delta_a = min{1/4, pi/(8 I_a)}` of
+`L:complex-phase` (lines 2298-2299), with `I_a` proved integrable and
+positive for `a < 2` (the TeX uses `a = alpha/2` in `(0,1)`), so `delta_a`
+is a genuine positive number; `A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2)`
+(lines 2585-2587); `d_N = 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R_alpha)` of `E:fock-sandwich`
+(lines 2484-2488).
+
+Steps (nothing supplied): Cauchy's estimate for an entire map with values
+in a complete complex normed space, operator-valued included (lines
+2616-2624), and the coefficient bound `||C_n|| <= M (d/c)^n` in the TeX's
+form, quantified over every `d' >= d`, `d' > 0` (this covers the TeX's
+`R_alpha = 0` case of line 2608 without dividing by zero); the arithmetic at
+`lambda = n/h` (lines 2631-2641): `d_n <= 2 sqrt(2n) sqrt(R)`, the display of
+lines 2636-2638, `100 n <= 200^n`, `n! <= n^n`; the pointwise Fourier
+multiplier form of the norm comparisons of lines 2632-2633 (the integration
+against the Fourier transform is not formalized); the exponent identity of
+`E:all-static-phase-sum`.
+
+Step rows. `E:all-static-phase-orders` at fixed cutoffs
+(`static_phase_order_cutoff`) and after both cutoff removals
+(`static_phase_all_orders_step`, wrapper `static_phase_all_orders_paper`),
+and `E:all-static-phase-sum` (`all_static_phase_sum_step`, wrapper
+`all_static_phase_sum_paper`). Abstractions: a complex Banach space stands
+for the cutoff space `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)` and a real Banach space for
+`L^2(Omega; X_(1/h))`; the phase propagator is an entire map `F` from the
+complex coupling to the bounded operators, its argument `v` is the initial
+phase `S_b(f,g)` times the vacuum, and the phase norms are real numbers
+`z1`, `zc m b`, `z`, `N1` named by the inputs. The supplied inputs are:
+entireness of the phase entries in the coupling (lines 2616-2617); the
+circle bound `100 e^(2 lambda h)` from `L:fock-form` and `L:complex-phase`
+with `a = alpha/2` (lines 2611-2614), stated for every `d' >= d_n`,
+`d' > 0`, which `L:complex-phase` gives from the sandwich bound of
+`L:fock-form` (a sandwich bound with constant `d_N` holds with every larger
+constant); the identification of the coefficient with the cutoff Duhamel
+phase via `L:finite-word-cutoff` (lines 2625-2630) together with the norm
+comparison `||z||_(1/h) <= n ||z||_(n/h)` (line 2632); `||S_b(f,g)||_(n/h) <=
+||(f,g)||_(1/h)` (line 2633; the contraction `||S_b(f,g)||_lambda <=
+||(f,g)||_lambda` is implicit in the TeX); the cutoff removals `b ->
+infinity` and `m -> infinity` (lines 2643-2667) as convergence of the norms
+along natural-number cutoffs (the TeX proves strong convergence, which
+implies it); and the free bound `||Z_0(h)||_(1/h) <= sqrt(e) ||(f,g)||_(1/h)`
+(line 2679). No input assumes a conclusion.
+
+The wrappers state the section's standing class as in
+`IntervalScalar.static_interaction_paper` (lines 2054-2066): locally finite
+`mu, Gamma` on `R^3`, `0 < alpha < 2`, `R = R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2
+sin(pi alpha/2))`; evenness, positive definiteness and scaling of `Gamma`
+enter only through the supplied inputs. Carried and not used (underscore
+hypotheses, confirmed by the proofs): in `static_phase_all_orders_paper`,
+local finiteness of `mu` and `Gamma`, `0 < alpha` and the formula for `R`
+(the step holds for every real `R` and `alpha < 2`); in
+`all_static_phase_sum_paper`, local finiteness (`0 < alpha` and the formula
+for `R` are used there, to get `0 <= alpha` and `R_alpha >= 0`).
+
+Junk values: `delta_a` is not a junk value (`I_a` is a proved-integrable
+positive integral); every real power has a positive base or a nonnegative
+base with a positive exponent; there is no division by `d_N`; summability
+is proved, not assumed through `tsum`. `sqrt(R)` is the real square root;
+in the wrappers `R = R_alpha >= 0`.
+
+Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the regularized Duhamel phases
+`Z_n^eps(h)` themselves, their being Gaussian polynomials of degree at most
+`n`, the uniformity in `eps` (it is that of the inputs), the convergence of
+`sum sigma^n Z_n^eps(h)` as an `L^2` phase identified with the Duhamel
+series (Lean proves absolute convergence of the abstract series), and the
+lemmas `L:fock-form`, `L:complex-phase` and the cutoff-removal arguments.
+The conclusions are the two displays for the quantities named by the
+inputs.

+## SymplecticFree (whole result)
+
+Formalizes the abstract core of `L:symplectic-free` (Free wave form and
+compact Young baseline) of `notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` at
+`a284420` (statement lines 30-60, proof lines 62-133; all line numbers in
+this section refer to that file). The lemma is an operator statement on
+`E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2)`; every row below is either a finite or
+operator-theoretic step proved with nothing supplied, or a statement about
+the free group that takes the supplied structure `FreeWaveData` (class
+inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement).
+
+What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix `W_t(xi)` of lines
+70-78 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
+quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix
+`[[1, t], [0, 1]]`; determinant one and `W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp` at every
+frequency, zero included (lines 79-81), the per-frequency group law and the
+reversal identity `R W_t R = W_(-t)` (lines 120-122). At nonzero frequency
+the matrix is the forward matrix of `DimensionalMatrix`
+(`freeMatrix_eq_forward`). (2) The force skewness of lines 40-41 and 88-91:
+abstractly for a bilinear pairing that is symmetric through the force
+(`omega_force_skew`), and at the `L^2` level on `R^d` with the integrability
+of the cancellation integrand (`omegaL2_force_skew`,
+`integrable_mul_force`). (3) The operator steps of the two compact
+baselines: closedness of the compact ideal along a nontrivial filter, each
+left Young sum compact, telescoping of ordered products, a compact operator
+maps a bounded weakly null family to a norm-null one, the abstract bound
+`||S|| <= ||S + K||` for `S` commuting with weakly null isometries, and
+`1 <= ||A||` from `B A = I`, `B = R A R`. (4) The two displays
+`E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline` (lines 45-49) and
+`E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline` (lines 53-58) in general form and as
+exact-hypothesis wrappers, and their conjunction with the per-frequency
+identity and the `L^2` force skewness (`symplectic_free_paper`).
+
+Abstractions and supplied inputs. `E` is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert
+space. `FreeWaveData d E` (D8) carries the free group `S_E` (`S_E(0) = I`,
+group law), an isometry `R` with `S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R`, and isometries
+`tau_y`, `y` in `R^d`, commuting with every `S_E(h)` and weakly null along
+the cocompact filter of `R^d`: exactly the properties that lines 103-122
+state for the free wave group, the velocity reversal `(u,v) -> (u,-v)` and
+the spatial translations (the weak nullity is the Riemann-Lebesgue argument
+of lines 105-110). `LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t` (D7) stands for
+`P:constant-young-linear` applied on `L(E)` (lines 91-98): along some
+nontrivial filter of partitions of `[s,t]`, the left Young sums of `X`
+converge in operator norm to `U(t,s) - I`; convergence as the mesh tends to
+zero implies it, so it is no stronger than its source. The Young evolution
+itself is not constructed: `U` is any operator family with this property.
+The wrappers take `H:homog` as the standing hypothesis; it is used only
+through `d >= 1`.
+
+Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `E != 0` (on the zero space every
+operator has norm `0`, and `||S_E(h)|| >= 1` fails), `d >= 1` (from
+`H:homog`; it makes the cocompact filter nontrivial), and the partition
+points lying in `[s,t]`. Hypotheses carried but unused (stated in the
+wrappers' doc comments and confirmed by their proofs): `theta`, the Hoelder
+bounds, `X(0) = 0` and `T > 0` (they are the hypotheses of the supplied
+Young input) in both baseline wrappers; `H:homog` and smoothness beyond
+continuity in `symplectic_force_skew_paper`.
+
+Proof-route differences: the compact-maps-weakly-null step (lines 110-112)
+is proved along an arbitrary filter through cluster points in the compact
+closure of the image of a ball and the adjoint, not by subsequences; the
+norm bound of lines 114-119 is proved for each `z` by a limit along the
+filter; the per-frequency symplecticity goes through `M^T J_symp M = (det M)
+J_symp` for every `2 x 2` matrix. Helpers that serve only this route are
+labelled auxiliary.
+
+Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the operator `J_E` (bounded,
+isometric, skew-adjoint, `J_E^2 = -I`), the identity `omega = <., J_E .>_E`
+with its duality form (lines 32-39, 63-68), the preservation of `omega` by
+`S_E` on all of `E` (the Fourier integration of the per-frequency identity,
+lines 82-86), the identification of the `H^(1/2)`-`H^(-1/2)` duality with
+the `L^2` integral and the estimate `||bu||_(H^(-1/2)) <=
+||b||_infinity ||u||_(H^(1/2))` (line 88), the construction of `S_E`,
+`tau_y` and the reversal with the properties of `FreeWaveData`, the Young
+evolution, and the remark that a zero length gives `P_j = I` (lines 129-130).
+The two displays are stated exactly as in the TeX, for the supplied objects.

  1174	+## SymplecticFree (whole result)
  1175	+
  1176	+Formalizes the abstract core of `L:symplectic-free` (Free wave form and
  1177	+compact Young baseline) of `notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` at
  1178	+`a284420` (statement lines 30-60, proof lines 62-133; all line numbers in
  1179	+this section refer to that file). The lemma is an operator statement on
  1180	+`E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2)`; every row below is either a finite or
  1181	+operator-theoretic step proved with nothing supplied, or a statement about
  1182	+the free group that takes the supplied structure `FreeWaveData` (class
  1183	+inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement).
  1184	+
  1185	+What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix `W_t(xi)` of lines
  1186	+70-78 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
  1187	+quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix
  1188	+`[[1, t], [0, 1]]`; determinant one and `W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp` at every
  1189	+frequency, zero included (lines 79-81), the per-frequency group law and the
  1190	+reversal identity `R W_t R = W_(-t)` (lines 120-122). At nonzero frequency
  1191	+the matrix is the forward matrix of `DimensionalMatrix`
  1192	+(`freeMatrix_eq_forward`). (2) The force skewness of lines 40-41 and 88-91:
  1193	+abstractly for a bilinear pairing that is symmetric through the force
  1194	+(`omega_force_skew`), and at the `L^2` level on `R^d` with the integrability
  1195	+of the cancellation integrand (`omegaL2_force_skew`,
  1196	+`integrable_mul_force`). (3) The operator steps of the two compact
  1197	+baselines: closedness of the compact ideal along a nontrivial filter, each
  1198	+left Young sum compact, telescoping of ordered products, a compact operator
  1199	+maps a bounded weakly null family to a norm-null one, the abstract bound
  1200	+`||S|| <= ||S + K||` for `S` commuting with weakly null isometries, and
  1201	+`1 <= ||A||` from `B A = I`, `B = R A R`. (4) The two displays
  1202	+`E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline` (lines 45-49) and
  1203	+`E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline` (lines 53-58) in general form and as
  1204	+exact-hypothesis wrappers, and their conjunction with the per-frequency
  1205	+identity and the `L^2` force skewness (`symplectic_free_paper`).
  1206	+
  1207	+Abstractions and supplied inputs. `E` is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert
  1208	+space. `FreeWaveData d E` (D8) carries the free group `S_E` (`S_E(0) = I`,
  1209	+group law), an isometry `R` with `S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R`, and isometries
  1210	+`tau_y`, `y` in `R^d`, commuting with every `S_E(h)` and weakly null along
  1211	+the cocompact filter of `R^d`: exactly the properties that lines 103-122
  1212	+state for the free wave group, the velocity reversal `(u,v) -> (u,-v)` and
  1213	+the spatial translations (the weak nullity is the Riemann-Lebesgue argument
  1214	+of lines 105-110). `LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t` (D7) stands for
  1215	+`P:constant-young-linear` applied on `L(E)` (lines 91-98): along some
  1216	+nontrivial filter of partitions of `[s,t]`, the left Young sums of `X`
  1217	+converge in operator norm to `U(t,s) - I`; convergence as the mesh tends to
  1218	+zero implies it, so it is no stronger than its source. The Young evolution
  1219	+itself is not constructed: `U` is any operator family with this property.
  1220	+The wrappers take `H:homog` as the standing hypothesis; it is used only
  1221	+through `d >= 1`.
  1222	+
  1223	+Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `E != 0` (on the zero space every
  1224	+operator has norm `0`, and `||S_E(h)|| >= 1` fails), `d >= 1` (from
  1225	+`H:homog`; it makes the cocompact filter nontrivial), and the partition
  1226	+points lying in `[s,t]`. Hypotheses carried but unused (stated in the
  1227	+wrappers' doc comments and confirmed by their proofs): `theta`, the Hoelder
  1228	+bounds, `X(0) = 0` and `T > 0` (they are the hypotheses of the supplied
  1229	+Young input) in both baseline wrappers; `H:homog` and smoothness beyond
  1230	+continuity in `symplectic_force_skew_paper`.

  1232	+Proof-route differences: the compact-maps-weakly-null step (lines 110-112)
  1233	+is proved along an arbitrary filter through cluster points in the compact
  1234	+closure of the image of a ball and the adjoint, not by subsequences; the
  1235	+norm bound of lines 114-119 is proved for each `z` by a limit along the
  1236	+filter; the per-frequency symplecticity goes through `M^T J_symp M = (det M)

5200	## SpatialStaticControls (whole result)
  5201	
  5202	Formalizes `L:spatial-static-controls` (Smooth temporal controls) of the
  5203	section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
  5204	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`): statement lines
  5205	40-54 (the definition of `lambda_z(c)^2`, lines 42-46; the display
  5206	`E:spatial-static-score`, lines 50-53), proof lines 56-96. The section's
  5207	standing assumptions (lines 4-10) are a nonzero covariance from `H:homog`
  5208	and `a = alpha0`; `U_z = Gamma * z` pointwise for smooth compact `z` (lines
  5209	37-38). The wrappers carry `HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and
  5210	`Gamma != 0`, and use the exponent `alpha0`.
  5211	
  5212	Objects. `lamSq U c` is `sSup` of the real Rayleigh set
  5213	(`WeakSobolev.rayleighSet`) of the potential `c U`, that is the supremum of
  5214	`c int U g^2 - ||grad g||_2^2` over unit `g` in `H^1(R^d;R)` (weak
  5215	gradients); `lam U c = sqrt (lamSq U c)` and `lamZ Gamma z = lam (Gamma * z)`
  5216	is `lambda_z`. The definition is the TeX's display with a general potential;
  5217	for the bounded potentials used here the side condition of
  5218	`WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic (`isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded`),
  5219	so the set is the manuscript's set. `I_Psi` and `v_Psi` are the package's
  5220	`VariationalDilation.integratedRate` (the integral of the real-Rayleigh rate)
  5221	and `VariationalDilation.rawCost` (the integral form of the cost); their
  5222	identification with `sqrt(-E_s)` and `E W(Psi)^2` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`,
  5223	`L:compact-raw-profile`) stays outside Lean, as for `VariationalDilation`.
  5224	`B_Gamma(z,z)` is `OccupationKernelRow.pairing` (the extended nonnegative
  5225	integral of `E:spatial-physical-pair`) at `zE z = ofReal o z`;
  5226	`pairing_bridge` proves it finite and equal to `ofReal (int z U_z)`, and the
  5227	statements use its `toReal` only after that. `M_a` is
  5228	`TemporalEquilibrium.mass` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-mass`) and `f_a` is
  5229	`TemporalEquilibrium.density`.
  5230	
  5231	Part (i). `spatial_static_controls_rate_paper` proves, for a nonnegative
  5232	nonzero test function `z`: every `y -> z(x-y)` is `Gamma`-integrable; for
  5233	`c > 0` the Rayleigh set of `c U_z` is nonempty and bounded above (so
  5234	`lambda_z(c)^2` is a finite supremum), `0 < lambda_z(c)^2`, `0 < lambda_z(c)`;
  5235	and `lambda_z` is Lipschitz on every `[c_1, c_2]` with `c_1 > 0`. The general
  5236	form `static_rate` also gives `|lambda_z(c)^2 - lambda_z(c')^2| <= M |c - c'|`
  5237	for every upper bound `M` of `U_z` (the TeX's constant `||U_z||_inf`, lines
  5238	62-63) without any floor. Positivity rests on the named input
  5239	`RayleighFloor Gamma`: for every nonnegative nonzero test function `z`, the
  5240	Rayleigh set of `U_z` contains a positive value. It stands for the dilation
  5241	floor lemma of wave item L6-d at `V = Gamma * z`
  5242	(`VariationalFloor.rayleighSet_floor`); it is discharged under the section's
  5243	hypotheses in `SpatialOccupationCompleted` (`rayleighFloor_of_homog`, with the
  5244	completed wrapper `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper`). Disclosure: since `U_z` is bounded (proved here), this input
  5245	is equivalent to `lambda_z(1)^2 > 0` for every such `z`, that is to the
  5246	positivity claim of part (i) itself; the Lean content of part (i) beyond the
  5247	input is the finiteness, the transfer of positivity to every `c > 0` (through
  5248	`Gamma * (c z) = c U_z`) and the Lipschitz bounds. The TeX's positivity route
  5249	is different: a positive rate of a smooth test with mean `c U_z` through
  5250	`P:variational-unmasked-rate` and `P:compact-original-common-trial` (lines
  5251	57-62). The input is satisfiable (`rayleighFloor_volume`: `Gamma` =
  5252	Lebesgue measure, an unrestricted constant covariance outside `H:homog`:
  5253	it scales like `c^d`, i.e. `alpha = 0`, and it is not spatial white noise,
  5254	which is `Gamma = delta_0`) and fails for `Gamma = 0` (refutation
  5255	`FloorZeroCovariance`). The boundedness of `U_z` comes from the Gaussian
  5256	envelope (`VariationalMean.conv_le`), not from `P:variational-unmasked-rate`
  5257	as in the TeX (lines 60-61).
  5258	
  5259	Part (ii). `spatial_static_score_paper` states `E:spatial-static-score` in
  5260	the existential form (the owner's decision 2 of wave L6): `B_Gamma(z,z)` is
  5261	finite, the Rayleigh set defining `lambda_z(1)` is nonempty and bounded
  5262	above, and every `y < lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z)` is exceeded by
  5263	`I_Psi - v_Psi/2` for some `Psi` in `C_pos` whose rate and time cost
  5264	integrand are integrable on `(0,1)`. This is equivalent to the TeX display
  5265	whenever `S_1^pos` is a finite supremum; `spatial_static_score_sSup_paper`
  5266	gives the display itself, `lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z) <= S_1^pos`, on
  5267	the named input `VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma` (boundedness above of
  5268	`VariationalRate.score1Set`, that is of
  5269	`{I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}`, word for word the boundedness claim of
  5270	`P:variational-positive-scores`, `integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines
  5271	272-274, whose manuscript proof, lines 309-325, uses `T:full-upper`; Lean
  5272	proves it deterministically in wave L8, `L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed`). Part
  5273	(ii) uses neither the floor nor `Gamma != 0`. The proof follows the TeX:
  5274	`Psi_n = f_n (x) z` (`ctrl`, in `C_pos` by `ctrl_mem`), mean
  5275	`k_n(s) U_z` (`mean_ctrl`), rate `lambda_z(k_n(s))` (`rate_ctrl`), cost
  5276	`(int_0^1 f_n k_n) int z U_z` (`rawCost_ctrl`), `k_n -> 1` with
  5277	`0 <= k_n <= 1` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-potential` via
  5278	`TemporalEquilibrium.potential_eq_one`), `int f_n k_n -> M_a`, and the
  5279	limit of the scores (`score_tendsto`); `ctrl_genuine` shows that every
  5280	Rayleigh set of `Psi_n` is nonempty and bounded and every integrand is
  5281	integrable, so no score is a junk value.
  5282	
  5283	Two bridges connect this module to `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`:
  5284	`pairing_eq_spatialPair` proves that the extended pairing
  5285	`OccupationKernelRow.pairing` and the real iterated integral
  5286	`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair` agree (and are finite) for continuous,
  5287	nonnegative, compactly supported functions and locally finite `Gamma`, and
  5288	`isUnitH1_of_unitTest` shows that a real unit test of `SpatialFourierBound`
  5289	with its classical gradient is a unit `H^1` pair. The weak gradient of a test
  5290	function (`VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test`), the radius lemma
  5291	(`VariationalFloor.exists_radius_fn`) and the score set, `S1Bdd`, `S1pos`
  5292	(`VariationalRate`) are shared with other modules and documented there.
  5293	
  5294	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: local finiteness of `Gamma` (`Gamma_radon`,
  5295	for Tonelli in `B_Gamma`); integrability of every integrand; nonemptiness and
  5296	boundedness of every Rayleigh set whose supremum is used; finiteness of
  5297	`B_Gamma(z,z)` before `toReal`. Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0` in
  5298	both wrappers (part (i) relies on it only through `RayleighFloor`), and the
  5299	fields of `H:homog` other than `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral`,
  5300	`Gamma_radon`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`.

  5303	`cut_n(t) = smoothTransition((n+4)t - 1) smoothTransition((n+4)(1-t) - 1)`
  5304	instead of `chi(1/(nt)) chi(1/(n(1-t)))` (lines 66-72); `fn = f_a cut_n`
  5305	has the properties the proof uses (smooth, vanishing near the endpoints,

5306	nonzero, `0 <= f_n <= f_a`, `f_n -> f_a`); monotonicity in `n` is not proved
  5307	or used; (2) dominated convergence replaces the monotone convergence of
  5308	lines 75-77 and 87-88; (3) the TeX's floor `c_0 <= k_n(s)` (line 78) is not
  5309	needed, because `lambda_z^2` is globally Lipschitz and `lambda_z` therefore
  5310	continuous on `R` (`lam_continuous`); (4) the mean and cost of `f_n (x) z` are
  5311	unconditional identities of Bochner integrals. Not formalized: the positivity
  5312	of `B_Gamma(z,z)` (lines 88-91), which the stated bound does not need; the

  5315	(`rayleighSet_const`, `lamSq_const`) support the satisfiability check and

  6277	## UniformSeriesTail (whole result)
  6278	
  6279	Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  6280	at `a284420`; statement lines 3703-3727 with the display
  6281	`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3718-3724; proof lines 3729-3748), with every
  6282	conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
  6283	3600-3645), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
  6284	facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731): absolute `L^2` convergence of
  6285	every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
  6286	states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
  6287	`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
  6288	complex `r`, lines 3643-3644) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
  6289	formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
  6290	and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3638-3641). Nothing else about the Gaussian
  6291	field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
  6292	statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
  6293	two facts. For the chain integrals `Y_n` of a centered Gaussian field with
  6294	nonnegative covariance, `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (wave L8)
  6295	proves `TerminalWickInput` from that lemma's own inputs, and
  6296	`L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the two; the
  6297	identification of the regularized family `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with such terms is
  6298	not formalized. The
  6299	fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
  6300	`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
  6301	`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
  6302	integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
  6303	product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
  6304	`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
  6305	`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
  6306	real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
  6307	`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
  6308	`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
  6309	`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
  6310	the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
  6311	such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
  6312	convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
  6313	in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
  6314	`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
  6315	absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
  6316	convergence", lines 3735-3736). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
  6317	last sentence (lines 3725-3726): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
  6318	`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
  6319	(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
  6320	used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
  6321	`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
  6322	space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
  6323	hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
  6324	bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
  6325	dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
  6326	are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
  6327	`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
  6328	(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
  6329	`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
  6330	(lines 3738-3745), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
  6331	the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
  6332	hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
  6333	`tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so
  6334	`Real.sqrt B` is the true square root; `r > 1` makes `(r^n)^(-1)` and

  6337	lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs; `L:terminal-wick` is in

  6901	## WaveGreen (whole result)
  6902	
  6903	Defines the wave Green measures `G_s` of the main file
  6904	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`) and states
  6905	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lemma, lines 803-848; proof, lines 849-919)
  6906	with nothing supplied. Sources of the measures at `a284420`: `d = 1`,
  6907	`G(s,y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s}` (proof of `L:white-test`, line 746; again at
  6908	lines 4128 and 7642); `d = 2, 3`, the proof of `L:higher-riesz` (lines
  6909	5179-5187), which quotes Chen (2.5), p. 7:
  6910	`G_h^(2)(dy) = 1_{|y|<h} dy / (2 pi sqrt(h^2 - |y|^2))` and
  6911	`G_h^(3)(dy) = sigma_h(dy)/(4 pi h)`, `sigma_h` the surface measure of the
  6912	radius-`h` sphere, and states "Both have mass `h` and satisfy
  6913	`G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)`" (lines 5186-5187). The list of notation
  6914	(`notes/index/list-of-notation.tex`, line 102) describes `G_t` as the "Wave
  6915	Green measure, with mass `t` and support in the closed radius-`t` ball". The
  6916	mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` is the step of the proof of
  6917	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` at line 881, which `DampedNormsHomog` took as
  6918	the supplied input `GreenMass G`.
  6919	
  6920	Definition. `waveGreen d s` is, for `d = 1`, `(1/2)` Lebesgue measure
  6921	restricted to the open ball `|x| < s`; for `d = 2`, Lebesgue measure with
  6922	density `1_{|x|<s} (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - |x|^2))^(-1)` (inside the ball the root
  6923	is of a positive number, so no `sqrt` or division junk value enters); for
  6924	`d = 3`, `(s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) volume.toSphere`; for every other `d`,
  6925	the zero measure. For `d = 3` this is a DEFINITIONAL CHOICE (Le's decision 4
  6926	for wave L6): Mathlib's `Measure.toSphere` (which satisfies
  6927	`sigma(A) = 3 vol{r w : 0 < r < 1, w in A}` for measurable `A`, the cone
  6928	measure) is taken as the surface measure of the unit sphere, and
  6929	`sigma_s = s^2 map (w -> s w) sigma_1` as that of the radius-`s` sphere, so
  6930	`sigma_s/(4 pi s) = (s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) sigma_1`. Neither
  6931	identification with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure is proved.
  6932	The manuscript has `d in {1,2,3}` (`H:homog`) and `s >= 0`; the value zero for
  6933	other `d` and for `s <= 0` is a Lean convention (`waveGreen_other`,
  6934	`waveGreen_of_nonpos`), and every mass and scaling statement carries
  6935	`d = 1 \/ d = 2 \/ d = 3`, so no statement holds through it.
  6936	
  6937	Formalized, all proved, nothing supplied: the mass `G_s(R^d) = s` for
  6938	`d in {1,2,3}` and every `s >= 0` (`waveGreen_mass`; `s = 0` included, where
  6939	the measure is zero); finiteness for every `d` and `s`; support in the closed
  6940	radius-`s` ball, `G_s((closedBall 0 s)^c) = 0`, for every `d` and `s`; the
  6941	scaling `G_s(sA) = s G_1(A)` for `s > 0` and measurable `A`
  6942	(`waveGreen_scaling`; the TeX does not say which sets `A`, and Borel sets are
  6943	the reading used; for `d = 1` it holds for every set, `scaling_one`, and
  6944	`d = 1` is included although the TeX states the scaling for `d = 2, 3`);

   290	The regularized terms are the terminal-chain integrals of `L:terminal-wick`,
   291	`Y^{ε,δ}_n = chainIntegral (ν ε δ) (hW ε δ) n`, for a centered real Gaussian field
   292	`W ε δ` on `[0,T] × ℝ^d` with covariance `K ε δ`.  For every `ε, δ > 0` the
   293	supplied structure `UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput` (absolute `L²` convergence of
   294	`Σ r^n Y^{ε,δ}_n` and nonnegative mixed moments) is proved by
   295	`TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` from `K ε δ ≥ 0`, so
   296	`UniformSeriesTail.uniform_series_tail_paper` applies with its hypothesis `hTW`
   297	discharged.  The conclusions are those of `uniform_series_tail_paper` (absolute
   298	convergence of `Σ X_n`, `u^{ε,δ}(1) → u`, the term and tail bounds of
   299	`E:uniform-series-tail`, absolute convergence of each `Σ Y^{ε,δ}_n`).

   302	bound `E|u^{ε,δ}(r)|² ≤ B` (`hB`) and the fixed-order limits `Y^{ε,δ}_n → X_n` (`hX`);

   307	the measurability of `K` of `TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper` are not needed for these
   308	two facts and are not taken.  The chain measures may depend on `(ε, δ)`; the TeX's
   309	fixed `g_n^{T,x}` is the constant case.  The field is given for every real pair
   310	`(ε, δ)` (a Lean device so that `Y` is a total function); only positive pairs enter
   311	the other hypotheses and the conclusions. -/

   313	    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (T : ℝ)
   314	    (hT : 0 < T) (W : ℝ → ℝ → TerminalWick.Pt d T → Ω → ℝ)
   315	    (K : ℝ → ℝ → TerminalWick.Pt d T → TerminalWick.Pt d T → ℝ)
   316	    (hW : ∀ ε δ, FiniteWick.CenteredGaussianField (W ε δ) (K ε δ) P)
   317	    (hVfin : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K ε δ p p))
   318	    (ν : ℝ → ℝ → ∀ n : ℕ, Measure (Fin n → TerminalWick.Pt d T))
   319	    [∀ ε δ n, IsFiniteMeasure (ν ε δ n)]
   320	    (hmass : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ n, ν ε δ n Set.univ = TerminalWick.chainMass d n T)
   321	    (hmeas : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ n,
   322	      AEStronglyMeasurable (fun z : Fin n → TerminalWick.Pt d T => TerminalWick.prodL2 (hW ε δ) z)
   323	        (ν ε δ n))
   324	    (hKpos : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ p q, 0 ≤ K ε δ p q)
   325	    (X : ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 P) (r B : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r)
   326	    (hB : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ →
   327	      ∫ ω, ((∑' n, r ^ n • TerminalWick.chainIntegral (ν ε δ) (hW ε δ) n : Lp ℝ 2 P) ω) ^ 2

   329	    (hX : ∀ n, Filter.Tendsto
   330	      (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => TerminalWick.chainIntegral (ν p.1 p.2) (hW p.1 p.2) n)

   332	    (Summable fun n => ‖X n‖) ∧
   333	      Filter.Tendsto (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ∑' n, TerminalWick.chainIntegral (ν p.1 p.2) (hW p.1 p.2) n)
   334	        (nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0) ×ˢ nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0))
   335	        (nhds (∑' n, X n)) ∧
   336	      (∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ n,
   337	        ‖TerminalWick.chainIntegral (ν ε δ) (hW ε δ) n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹) ∧

   342	      (∀ N : ℕ, ‖∑' n, X (n + (N + 1))‖ ≤
   343	        Real.sqrt B * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) ∧
   344	      (∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ →
   345	        Summable fun n => ‖TerminalWick.chainIntegral (ν ε δ) (hW ε δ) n‖) := by
   346	  refine UniformSeriesTail.uniform_series_tail_paper
   347	    (fun ε δ n => TerminalWick.chainIntegral (ν ε δ) (hW ε δ) n) X r B hr
   348	    (fun ε δ hε hδ => ?_) hB hX

   356	  exact TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg (ν ε δ) (hW ε δ) _ hV0 hV
   357	    (hmeas ε δ hε hδ) T hmassR (hKpos ε δ hε hδ) r

   361	/-- Auxiliary (Lean proof route): a real function tends to `0` along a filter if, for
   362	every `ε > 0`, it lies within `ε` of a function that tends to `0`. -/
   363	private theorem tendsto_zero_of_forall_approx {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {F : ι → ℝ}
   364	    (h : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ G : ι → ℝ, Filter.Tendsto G l (nhds 0) ∧ ∀ i, |F i - G i| ≤ ε) :
   365	    Filter.Tendsto F l (nhds 0) := by
   366	  rw [Metric.tendsto_nhds]
   367	  intro ε hε
   368	  obtain ⟨G, hG, hFG⟩ := h (ε / 2) (by positivity)
   369	  filter_upwards [Metric.tendsto_nhds.mp hG (ε / 2) (by positivity)] with i hi
   370	  rw [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero] at hi ⊢
   371	  calc |F i| = |(F i - G i) + G i| := by ring_nf
   372	    _ ≤ |F i - G i| + |G i| := abs_add_le _ _
   373	    _ < ε := by linarith [hFG i]

     2	\label{S:spatial-occupation-foundation}

     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}
    34	
    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.

    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{lemma}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  Choose nonnegative nonzero $f \in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ and $s_0 = 1/2$. Let
    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.
    65	
    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]
    73	  Extend $f_n$ by zero. It is smooth compact, vanishes near both endpoints, is
    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.
    82	
    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.
    86	  \]
    87	  Its time integrand increases to $f_a$, so the cost tends to
    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.
    91	  Such a ball exists by exhaustion. Take the limit of the individual
    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves
    95	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls}.
    96	\end{proof}

   101	\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy]
   102	  \label{L:spatial-fourier-bound}
   103	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, allowing $\Gamma=0$, let
   104	  $g\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R)$ satisfy $\|g\|_2=1$ and put
   105	  $b=\|\nabla g\|_2^2$. Then $b>0$ and
   106	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-fourier-bound}
   107	    0\le A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)
   108	    \le 2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2},
   109	  \end{equation}
   110	  where $R_\alpha$ is defined in~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}.
   111	\end{lemma}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  If $b=0$, smoothness makes $\nabla g=0$ everywhere. Thus, $g$ is constant,
   115	  and compact support forces $g=0$, contrary to $\|g\|_2=1$. Put $Q=g^2$ and
   116	  use the unnormalized Fourier transform
   117	  \[
   118	    \mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)=\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x.
   119	  \]
   120	  In the unitary convention of Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance}, this is
   121	  $c_d^{-1}\widehat Q$, with $c_d=(2\pi)^{-d/2}$.
   122	  The autocorrelation
   123	  \[
   124	    c_Q(y)=\int_{\R^d}Q(x)Q(x-y)\ud x
   125	  \]
   126	  is smooth and compactly supported. Apply the distributional spectral
   127	  identity~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to this Schwartz function.
   128	  Its inner Fourier integral is $|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2$, since $Q$ is real.
   129	  Hence
   130	  \[
   131	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\int c_Q(y)\Gamma(\ud y)
   132	    =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   133	  \]
   134	  Both integrals are finite: $c_Q$ is compactly supported and $\Gamma$ is
   135	  Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   136	  No density of either measure is required.
   137	
   138	  Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   139	  and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   140	  \[
   141	    |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   142	    \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   143	    \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   144	  \]
   145	  Splitting into $|\xi|^2\le4b$ and $|\xi|^2>4b$ therefore yields
   146	  \[
   147	    |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.
   148	  \]
   149	  The deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
   150	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together
   151	  with~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}, gives, for $q>0$,
   152	  \[
   153	    \mathcal{R}_\Gamma(q):=\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{q^2+|\xi|^2}
   154	    =q^{\alpha-2}R_\alpha<\infty.
   155	  \]
   156	  Consequently,
   157	  \[
   158	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   159	    =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.
   160	  \]
   161	  Nonnegativity follows from the spectral identity. If $\Gamma=0$, then
   162	  $\mu=0$ and both sides of~\eqref{E:spatial-fourier-bound} vanish. This proves
   163	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound}.
   164	\end{proof}
   165	
   166	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
   167	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   168	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   169	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   170	  a positive finite real number, and
   171	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   172	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   173	    k\left[
   174	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   175	    \right]^{1/k}.
   176	  \end{equation}
   177	\end{proposition}
   178	
   179	\begin{proof}
   180	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero
   181	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   182	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   183	  autocorrelation argument in the proof of
   184	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} gives
   185	  $0 < A:=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)<\infty$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound} gives
   186	  $R(g)\le2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha$ for every such profile. A normalized compact
   187	  bump supplies a positive ratio. Thus, $0<R_0<\infty$, independently of the
   188	  finiteness of $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$. It remains to prove the score inequality.
   189	  With $U_\ell g(x)=\ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the physical changes of variables give
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   191	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   192	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   195	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   196	
   197	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   198	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   199	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   200	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   201	  \[
   202	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   203	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   204	  \]
   205	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   206	  gives
   207	  \[
   208	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   209	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   210	  \]
   211	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   212	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   213	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. This argument retains the finite
   214	  real value $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ fixed at the start of the section; only the
   215	  proof of $R_0<\infty$ is independent of that input. This proves
   216	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   217	\end{proof}

   219	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   220	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   221	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   222	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   223	  \begin{align}
   224	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   225	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   226	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   227	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   228	  \end{align}
   229	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   230	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   232	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   233	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   234	  \end{equation}
   235	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   236	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   237	\end{proposition}
   238	
   239	\begin{proof}
   240	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   241	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   242	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   243	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   244	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   245	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   246	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   247	  convention gives
   248	  \[
   249	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   250	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   251	  \]
   252	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   253	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   254	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   255	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   256	  \[
   257	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   258	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   259	  \]
   260	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   261	
   262	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   263	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   264	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   265	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   266	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   267	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   268	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   269	
   270	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   271	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   272	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   273	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   274	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   275	  continuity.
   276	
   277	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   278	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   279	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   280	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   281	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   282	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   283	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   284	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   285	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   286	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   287	
   288	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   289	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   290	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   291	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   292	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   293	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   294	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   295	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   296	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   297	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   298	\end{proof}

   300	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   301	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   302	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   303	  \[
   304	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   305	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   306	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   307	  \]
   308	  Then
   309	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   310	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   311	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   312	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   313	    \in(0,\infty).
   314	  \end{equation}
   315	  In particular,
   316	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   317	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   318	    \qquad
   319	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   320	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   321	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   322	  \end{equation}
   323	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   324	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   325	\end{proposition}
   326	
   327	\begin{proof}
   328	  Physical change of variables, or smooth approximation and
   329	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, extends \eqref{E:spatial-dilation} to
   330	  real $H^1$ profiles. For fixed unit $g$, with $A,b > 0$, the maximum of
   331	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals
   332	  \[
   333	    \frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   334	    R(g)^{2/(2-\alpha)}.
   335	  \]
   336	  Dilation preserves the whole unit class and includes $\ell = 1$. Taking both
   337	  numerical suprema, then profiles with ratio tending to $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$,
   338	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. No optimizer is assumed. Smooth ratios
   339	  also approach $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   340	  Pass them through~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score} and substitute
   341	  \[
   342	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}\alpha^{\alpha/2}
   343	    =\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2-\alpha}
   344	    \right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}.
   345	  \]
   346	  This gives~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. This proves
   347	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-energy-map}.
   348	\end{proof}

1	\section{The unmasked Rayleigh rate and nonnegative controls}
     2	\label{S:unmasked-variational}
     3	
     4	Fix a nonzero covariance satisfying Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, including its
     5	original amplitude, and set $a = \alpha_0$. Define the full class
     6	\begin{equation}\label{E:variational-positive-class}
     7	  \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}
     8	  =\{\Psi\in C_c^\infty((0,1)\times\R^d;\R):
     9	  \Psi\ge0,\ \Psi\ne0\}.
    10	\end{equation}
    11	
    12	\input{notes/figures/nonseparable-controls}
    13	It includes nonseparable tests. It is nonempty: if $b(z) = e^{-1/(1-z^2)}$ on
    14	$|z| < 1$ and zero otherwise, then $b(4s-2)\prod_{j=1}^db(x_j)$ belongs to this
    15	class. All boundary derivatives vanish because exponential decay dominates every
    16	power of $(1-z^2)^{-1}$. For each $\Psi$ retain the original mean $h_{\Psi,s}$
    17	and original variance $v_\Psi = \E W(\Psi)^2$ from~\eqref{E:compact-raw-mean}--%
    18	\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Neither the test nor its covariance is changed by a
    19	physical mask. We write $h_s$ when $\Psi$ is fixed.
    20	
   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}

    23	\begin{lemma}[Full-profile squares in the original space]
    24	  \label{L:occupation-raw-square}

    26	  \[
    27	    \langle Q(f),Q(h)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    28	    =B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2),\qquad
    29	    \|Q(f)\|^2=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f).
    30	  \]
    31	  For $g \in \mathcal{O}$, the element $\rho_g = J_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}(s\mapsto
    32	  Q(g_s))$ belongs to the original $H_I$ and satisfies
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-raw-identities}
    34	    \|\rho_g\|_{H_I}^2=A(g),\qquad
    35	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}
    36	    =\int_I\int_{\R^d}h_{\Psi,s}(x)g_s(x)^2\ud x\ud s
    37	  \end{equation}
    38	  for every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$. In particular,
    39	  \[
    40	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}\le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g)}.
    41	  \]

    46	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} gives
    47	  \[
    48	    \|f_n^2-f_l^2\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}^2
    49	    =C_4(f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l,f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l)
    50	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}N(f_n-f_l)^2N(f_n+f_l)^2\to0.
    51	  \]
    52	  Here $N$ is continuous on $H^1$ and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. Completeness
    53	  defines $Q(f)$; interlacing two approximating sequences proves independence.
    54	  Passing the physical four-linear continuity and Hilbert pairings to limits
    55	  proves the first identities. The same difference bound, first for smooth
    56	  approximants and then by passage to the limit, proves continuity of $Q$.
    57	
    58	  Thus, $F_g(s) = Q(g_s)$ is strongly measurable. Writing $b_s = \|\nabla
    59	  g_s\|_2^2$, the unit norm and $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$ give
    60	  \[
    61	    \int_I\|F_g(s)\|^2\ud s
    62	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}\int_I b_s^{\alpha/2}\ud s
    63	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty .
    64	  \]

    66	  its squared norm with the physical $A(g)$. Joint measurability and
    67	  representative independence follow from the continuous physical pairing on
    68	  $(H^1)^2$. Absolute time integrability follows from the same Schur bound.
    69	
    70	  Choose one compact smooth $\chi$ equal to one on all spatial supports of
    71	  $\Psi_t$. For real $f \in H^1$, smooth approximation gives
    72	  \[
    73	    \langle\Psi_t,Q(f)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    74	    =\lim_n B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f_n^2)
    75	    =C_4(\chi,\Psi_t,f,f)=B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f^2).

    92	\begin{proposition}[Original occupation energy and dilation]
    93	  \label{P:raw-occupation-energy}
    94	  With $K_0 = 2^a/(1-a)$,
    95	  \[
    96	    0<C_{\rm occ}\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty .
    97	  \]
    98	  Moreover,
    99	  \begin{align}
   100	    \mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}
   101	    &=D_\zeta C_{\rm occ}^{2/(2-\alpha)},&
   102	    D_\zeta&=\frac{2-\alpha}{2}
   103	    \left(\frac{\alpha}{2\zeta}\right)^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)},
   104	    \label{E:raw-occupation-energy}\\
   105	    C_{\rm occ}
   106	    &=\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}}{2-\alpha}\right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}
   107	    \left(\frac{2\zeta}{\alpha}\right)^{\alpha/2}.
   108	    \label{E:raw-occupation-ratio}
   109	  \end{align}

   111	  $\zeta^{-\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_1^{\mathcal{O}}$.

   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  A unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy: a zero weak gradient makes
   116	  it constant, and an $L^2$ constant on $\R^d$ is zero. Hence, $0 < T(g) <
   117	  \infty$. Spatial covariance Cauchy--Schwarz gives $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   118	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}b_s^{\alpha/4}b_t^{\alpha/4}$. Schur with row bound $K_0$, then
   119	  concavity, proves
   120	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-occupation-bound}
   121	    0\le A(g)\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}.
   122	  \end{equation}
   123	  A fixed compact smooth unit profile, constant in time, belongs to
   124	  $\mathcal{O}$ and has positive $A$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   125	  This proves positivity and finiteness of $C_{\rm occ}$.
   126	
   127	  The map $(U_\ell g)_s(x) = \ell^{d/2}g_s(\ell x)$ is an $H^1$ isomorphism
   128	  preserving unit mass and strong measurability. It has inverse $U_{1/\ell}$ and
   129	  is a bijection on $\mathcal{O}$. The physical Radon change of variables gives
   130	  \[
   131	    A(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A(g),\qquad
   132	    T(U_\ell g)=\ell^2T(g).
   133	  \]
   134	  Indeed, the two densities contribute $\ell^{2d}$, $\ud x$ contributes
   135	  $\ell^{-d}$, and the pushforward of $\Gamma$ contributes $\ell^{\alpha-d}$.
   136	  Approximation extends the identity to full $H^1$. Taking the union over
   137	  $g,\ell$ leaves the class unchanged. For fixed $A,T > 0$, the derivative of
   138	  $A\ell^\alpha-\zeta T\ell^2$ has the sign of $\alpha A-2\zeta
   139	  T\ell^{2-\alpha}$. Its global maximum occurs at $\ell = (\alpha A/(2\zeta
   140	  T))^{1/(2-\alpha)}$ and equals $D_\zeta[A/T^{\alpha/2}]^{2/(2-\alpha)}$. For
   141	  $A = 0$ the supremum is zero as $\ell\downarrow0$. Bounding every ratio by
   142	  $C_{\rm occ}$ gives one inequality in~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-energy}. Fixed
   143	  ratios approaching its positive supremum give the other by continuity of the
   144	  positive power. Algebra gives~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-ratio} and the penalty
   145	  scaling. No optimizer or minimax interchange is assumed. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-occupation-energy}.
